ideas.risks: The best fixed quote comparator may collapse the construction: independent blocks can average into one Bayes-optimal quote, erasing accumulated per-block gaps. A full terminal reveal may also solve later blocks unless parameters are refreshed or localized.
ideas.summary: Design a multi-scale Le Cam/Fano lower bound that accumulates many q-scaled hidden-terminal atoms while keeping the world-specific best fixed quote separated from the posterior-mixture quote. A useful target is a dyadic construction with delays D_j, tail masses q_j near a prescribed envelope B(D_j), and hidden bits whose payoff-relevant quote intervals do not let one global reveal solve all scales.
ideas.title: Multi-Scale Hidden-Tail Lower Bounds
ideas.why_promising: The main open quantitative gap is matching the truncation upper rate under power tails. The accepted one-block atom is too weak; a multi-scale indistinguishability construction is the most direct route to a matching minimax lower bound.

ideas.risks: The meta-learner may pay delay overhead for the largest window rather than the selected window. Full-information feedback for unplayed base algorithms must be reconstructed cleanly, and comparator-gap truncation terms may not be monotone enough for a simple proof.
ideas.summary: Build a dyadic-window truncation algorithm competing with the best H in hindsight: run residue-Hedge base learners for H in {1,2,4,...}, compute each base learner's H-truncated reward after H future prices, and aggregate bases with a delayed full-information meta-learner. Aim for min_H {sqrt(T H log K)+T/K+delta_T(H)} plus polylog overhead.
ideas.title: Tail-Adaptive Truncation Algorithm
ideas.why_promising: The current upper bound requires choosing H from a tail profile. An adaptive version would strengthen the sufficient theorem and may reveal whether the present rate is algorithmic-artifact loose.

ideas.risks: Strict threshold rewards create nonattainment and discontinuities when conditional future-price laws have atoms. The result may require strong no-atom or semicontinuity assumptions and may not improve the core theorem.
ideas.summary: Investigate exact continuum Bayes/minimax formulas under regularity assumptions on conditional reward curves, instead of passing through grids. Identify minimal assumptions ensuring measurable epsilon-selectors or maximizers for a -> a P(M_t>a | P_1:t), then compare the continuum least-favorable-prior value to the established grid value.
ideas.title: Continuum Bayes Formula Under Regularity
ideas.why_promising: The current theorem package avoids continuum selector issues with O(T/K) discretization. A clean continuum theorem under natural atomlessness or regularity could simplify final statements and clarify which pathologies are purely grid artifacts.

ideas.risks: Identifiability may only give easy oracle-style policies rather than product compactness. Measurable selection of decoded known-law or Bayes-optimal quotes can fail without explicit standard-Borel assumptions.
ideas.summary: Prove a no-gap theorem for singular but identifiable classes: after a public Borel label Z(P_1:t0) reveals a parameter or fiber, each fiber is payoff-measure dominated or finite-class learnable, and the decoded policy is Borel measurable. Formalize this as an alternative to common domination of all reward measures.
ideas.title: Identifiable Singular No-Gap Classes
ideas.why_promising: Payoff-measure domination excludes many deterministic labeled classes that are actually easy. An identifiable-fiber theorem would extend the value characterization to natural nondominated examples without relying on non-Borel pathologies.

ideas.risks: A natural Borel gap may not exist under standard Borel public labels because Borel policies can often decode or uniformize the relevant relation. The search may turn into an impossibility theorem rather than a counterexample.
ideas.summary: Search for a Borel, nondominated, non-identifiable infinite class where every finite subclass has small grid value but the full Borel-policy value is linear. If none is found, try proving that standard Borel identifiable or analytic-payoff classes have no such gap via measurable selection or uniformization.
ideas.title: Natural Infinite-Class Gap Search
ideas.why_promising: The known finite-subclass/full-class obstruction is non-Borel and pathological. Finding or ruling out a natural Borel obstruction would clarify whether product-closure hypotheses are technical or substantively necessary.

ideas.risks: The resulting quantity may be almost as complex as the Bayes value itself, losing the appeal of a tail characterization. Lower bounds from the truncated Bayes gap may be hard to express as simple rates.
ideas.summary: Define a class-level predictability-weighted truncation modulus, such as the loss between the finite-grid Bayes gap Psi_G and its H-truncated analogue, and prove two-sided inequalities relating the full minimax value to the truncated minimax value plus this modulus. Test it on hidden/labeled and q-scaled terminal examples.
ideas.title: Predictability-Weighted Tail Modulus
ideas.why_promising: Scalar per-law tail profiles are refuted, but the upper theorem still uses truncation. A posterior/predictability-aware truncation modulus could bridge the accepted Bayes-value characterization with usable tail-rate statements.
